system.name: SymC
system.one_liner: A code model whose self-attention is equivariant to semantics-preserving statement permutations of the program dependence graph, so predictions stay invariant.

content.variant_note: the same code-to-name pipeline drawn twice, as a commutative-square diagram: ours keeps the permutation (tick), the existing model breaks it (cross)
content.argues: An equivariant representation under statement permutation g keeps the predicted function name invariant; a model that ignores g embeds the permuted code unrelatedly and predicts the wrong name.
content.subject: A four-line code snippet and its permuted copy, their embeddings and the predicted function name, drawn for SymC and for existing models.

new_tags.name: equivariance-square
new_tags.what: a commutative-diagram-like square in which the same transformation g is drawn on the input above and on the representation below, with tick versus cross showing whether the output stays invariant

lessons.what_to_learn: Draw an invariance claim as a commutative square: the transformation g on the input and the same g on the representation, one changed element tracked in red through both, ending in tick versus cross, while the baseline lane breaks the square (h ≠ g).
lessons.suits: Equivariance, invariance, augmentation or robustness claims where a transformation of the input should or should not change the output.

evidence: SYMC enforces its output to stay invariant via keeping its learned representation G-equivariant
(b) Code LLMs not preserving the symmetries in G and thus mispredict the label.

summary: SymC is a code model that builds the symmetry of semantics-preserving statement permutations into self-attention over the program dependence graph, so that tasks such as function name prediction stay invariant. Figure 1 contrasts two lanes on the same toy snippet (assert a > 0, assert b > 0, area = a * b, return area). In (a), swapping statements c1 and c2 by g gives permuted embeddings e2, e1, e3, e4 with unchanged colours, and the prediction map p returns 'calculate_area' with a green tick. In (b), an existing code LLM maps the permuted code to unrelated embeddings e'1..e'4 through an h that is not g and predicts 'check' with a red cross. The moved statement c1 is red throughout; dashed curves trace each line to its embedding.
summary_zh: SymC把保持语义的语句置换这一对称性写进注意力，使函数名预测对语句顺序不变。图1用同一段代码对比两栏：(a)置换g后嵌入同步变换，预测calculate_area打绿勾；(b)现有模型嵌入无关（h≠g），误判check打红叉。
notes: The prior primary kind (concept-schematic, formal-diagram) is kept as the second kind; the paired panels with tick versus cross make the contrast the primary message. Digest shows a single 9 pt bitmap; the two green ticks are vector fills (#2d9c5e).
